Chapter 8: Sustaining Growth Through Ongoing Practice
Overcoming bias isn’t something you check off a list—it’s really a lifelong journey. Think of it a bit like learning to play the guitar, or picking up a new language. It takes steady effort, a lot of patience, and the willingness to begin again, even when you slip up.
Sustaining real growth means making awareness, empathy, and repair part of your everyday life.
Here’s a helpful way to picture it: imagine bias work as your “mental fitness routine.” Just like you keep your body healthy with small, consistent habits, you keep your mind flexible and open with regular practice. So, what does that look like in real life?
Maybe it’s taking a few moments each day to reflect—just pausing and noticing when assumptions or biases pop up, and gently asking yourself where they might come from.
Or, you might set aside time each week to check in with a friend, a partner, or a group you trust. Share your challenges, your insights, and learn from each other.
Another powerful habit is inviting feedback. What if you could ask people to point out blindspots you might not see? And when they do, try meeting it with gratitude instead of getting defensive.
And of course, everyone makes mistakes. The key is to treat those moments as chances to grow, not as reasons to feel ashamed.
Here’s something we often forget: it’s important to celebrate progress, no matter how small. Did a conversation go a little smoother than usual? Did you welcome a new perspective, even if it challenged you? Those moments matter. Over time, they build up, creating real momentum and a sense of what’s possible.
Being gentle with yourself is part of this, too. Bias runs deep, and old habits can sneak back in, especially when you’re tired or stressed. When that happens, it’s okay to return to the basics—pause, reflect, and reconnect with empathy. Every day gives you a fresh start to practice.
In our relationships, this steady effort creates trust and safety. People start to feel seen and valued, even when they don’t agree on everything. In our communities, it helps build a culture of curiosity and respect.
The truth is, the journey never really ends. But every step you take brings a deeper sense of understanding—and a stronger connection to those around you.
